full_judgment:
Md Awlad Ali J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-02 (Annexure D) passed by the respondent No.1 in Title Suit No. 165/01 should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge and Altha Rin Adalat decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 14-5-02 (Annexure D). It has been contended by the petitioners that the Altha Rin Adalat acted beyond its jurisdiction as the loan amount claimed by the plaintiff respondent bank is not a loan as per definition of sub-section (2) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain and therefore, the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka is without jurisdiction. 

 "This Division has held in the case of Gannysons Ltd vs Sonali Bank and others, 36 DLR (AD) 146, that once a property vests in the Government under President's Order 16 of 1972 no legal proceedings can be taken against such property. The money decree obtained by Rupali Bank against Dr Shamim, the execution case thereof and the auction sale of the said property are all void and will not divest the Government of its title to the suit property and the auction purchaser has acquired no title to the same by his auction purchase." 

 8. Mr Saifuddin Ahmed Chowdhury, the learned Advocate representing the bank, has contended that the property was admittedly declared as abandoned property and that vested in the Government but the Government subsequently transferred the property with all its assets and liabilities including the bank liability and, as such, the petitioners are liable to pay the bank dues which was outstanding before the transfer. He has further argued that the property was mortgaged to the respondent bank and therefore the transfer made by the Government to the Trust is subject to mortgage and knowing full well about the bank liabilities the Welfare Trust contested the suit and the suit having been decreed the petitioners are liable to pay the decretal dues. H is further contention is that the claim of the bank was proved by sufficient evidence including the documentary evidence, the deed of transfer by which the property was transferred by the Government to the Welfare Trust and the decree being a contested decree the writ petitioner had efficacious alternative remedy under section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 by way of appeal and since there was alternative remedy available to the petitioner the writ petition is not maintainable. 

 11. Legal process as mentioned in Article 14 of President's Order 16 of 1972 includes also the summons in the suit and if it appeared from the plaint that the petitioner No. 1 purchased abandoned property process should not have been issued against the defendants who acquired the abandoned property with undetermined liabilities. If the decree that has been passed is not executable in view of the provision of Article 14 of President's Order 16 of 1972 and the principle expounded in the above cited decision then the impugned decree should not have been passed by the Adalat which leads to the irreversible conclusion that the decree is without jurisdiction and unauthorised under the law. In that view the Artha Rin Adalat had no jurisdiction to entertain the suit against the Bangladesh Freedom Fighters Welfare Trust and its officers and therefore, the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-02 is without jurisdiction.
